description: We are a team of four enthusiastic students passionate about space science, astronomy, and technology. We aim to solve real-world challenges using NASA’s open data through creativity, research, and innovation. We value teamwork, critical thinking, and learning. Together, we aspire to develop an impactful project and make our participation in the NASA Space Apps Challenge a meaningful experience.
summary: Lunar & Martian Legacies is an interactive educational storytelling platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten.” Our project explores human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars, presenting the stories behind their purposes, missions, exploration journeys, final status, and scientific contributions. By bringing this information together in an engaging digital experience, our platform helps visitors understand the history and legacy of space exploration beyond simply viewing abandoned objects. It addresses the challenge by making these often-overlooked stories easier to discover and understand. Our goal is to preserve the scientific legacy of past missions, make space knowledge more accessible, and inspire future explorers.
details:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive storytelling website about NASA's retired equipment on the Moon, Mars and in deep space, built by Team Terrestrial Lunars for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It asks "What happens to a machine when its mission ends?" and answers through a five-stage journey: The Question, The Mission, The Machine, The Discovery and The Legacy.

Users can follow a machine's story in 3D, explore a globe of the Moon and Mars, search an equipment database, browse a mission timeline, compare two machines, and test their knowledge in a Learning Hub. Every record cites NASA sources.

The project makes mission history engaging for students and space enthusiasts, shows that the science and lessons from these machines live on, and encourages responsible stewardship of human-made objects on other worlds. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on Netlify, and uses our own summaries of public NASA mission history (not live feeds). It is an independent educational project, not affiliated with NASA.
